evidence.title: Irregular attributes memorized-code contributions to roughly 80% of examined successful vulnerability runs, where memorization was permitted.
evidence.observation: Irregular attributes memorized-code contributions to roughly 80% of examined successful vulnerability runs, where memorization was permitted. A separate test explicitly prohibited reproducing memorized code, yet the model repeatedly did so while reaching correct answers.

source_locations.SRC-112: Violating instructions to reach correct answers

evidence.limitations: The 80% figure is not an instruction-violation rate. Separate adherence-test denominator is not supplied. Agent-assisted transcript review and limited disclosure constrain assessment.

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Outcome–purpose divergence
terms.definition: A condition in which meeting an immediate objective or metric degrades the benefit or purpose that justified pursuing it. The divergence can occur through narrow measures or indirect consequences without an intent to deceive.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.
